# Getting Started with the Inventory API

Welcome to the **Inventory API** documentation. This guide walks you through
setting up your development environment and making your first API calls.

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have the following installed:

- **Node.js** version 18 or later
- A running instance of *PostgreSQL* 15+
- An API key from the [developer portal](https://developers.example.com/keys)

## Authentication

All API requests require a valid bearer token. You can obtain one by sending
your API key to the authentication endpoint. Tokens expire after **24 hours**
and must be refreshed using the refresh token provided in the initial response.

For more details on token lifecycle management, see the
[authentication guide](https://docs.example.com/auth).

## Quick Start

First, install the client library using your preferred package manager:

```bash
npm install @example/inventory-client
```

Then initialize the client in your application:

```javascript
const client = new InventoryClient({
  apiKey: process.env.INVENTORY_API_KEY,
  baseUrl: "https://api.example.com/v2",
});
```

## Making Your First Request

Once authenticated, you can retrieve a list of products from your inventory.
The response includes pagination metadata, so you can iterate through large
result sets efficiently. Each product object contains its current stock level,
warehouse location, and pricing information.

If you encounter a `429 Too Many Requests` response, the API enforces a rate
limit of **100 requests per minute** per API key. Implement exponential backoff
in your retry logic to handle this gracefully.

## Next Steps

- Read the [full API reference](https://docs.example.com/api) for all endpoints
- Explore the [webhook integration guide](https://docs.example.com/webhooks)
- Join our [community forum](https://community.example.com) for support
